title: Netflix CEO admits app may bury stuff you want to watch under stuff you don’t
gist: In a Bloomberg interview, Netflix co-CEO Ted Sarandos said the streaming wars continue with half of US TV engagement still linear, admitted Netflix's app can bury content users want, and said Netflix must improve its US hit rate by betting on ambitious storytelling over AI 'slop' while expanding theatrical releases.

insights.claim: Netflix co-CEO Ted Sarandos says the streaming wars continue because half of US television engagement is still linear TV, though Nielsen data put streaming at 49.6% of TV viewing in August versus 36.4% for broadcast and cable.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Remaining linear viewing is the growth pool streamers still compete for.
insights.quote: Half of television engagement in the United States is still linear, old television,
insights.locator: “The streaming wars are continuing as we go.

insights.claim: Netflix reported over 325 million subscribers as of January, more than any other streaming service, and counts YouTube and Skydance among key rivals.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Netflix's scale lead is intact, shifting focus to engagement and hit quality.

insights.claim: Sarandos concedes Netflix should be doing better in the US and must focus on maintaining its hit rate as the business matures.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Watch US engagement and hit output as a key indicator of Netflix's content ROI.
insights.quote: we should be doing better in the US than we were
insights.locator: I think as Netflix has grown and matured

insights.claim: Netflix's reputation for must-watch exclusives, built in the Peak TV era, has weakened in the 2020s as viewers are inundated with content and struggle to find relevant titles.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Content glut erodes differentiation, raising the value of discovery and true hits.

insights.claim: Sarandos bets that audiences will want more ambitious, accomplished storytelling in a world flooded with AI 'slop', rather than chasing short-attention content.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Positions premium human-led content as a moat against cheap AI-generated video.
insights.quote: “I think what’s going to happen is that people will desire more ambitious, more accomplished storytelling in a world that is flooded with slop,”

insights.claim: Netflix has used generative AI workflows for production tasks such as crowds and historical battle scenes on hundreds of titles, saving money even as it raised content spending about 10% this year.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: GenAI is already a cost lever in Netflix production, supporting margins amid rising content spend.
insights.locator: Netflix has used generative AI-based workflows

insights.claim: Sarandos admitted Netflix's app can bury content viewers want under new titles they are not seeking, and pointed to AI as a tool for content discovery.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Recommendation/discovery improvements are a lever for engagement; watch for AI-driven UX changes.
insights.quote: bury things that you might be looking for under new things that you’re not coming for.
insights.locator: When it comes to streaming users struggling

insights.claim: Netflix is becoming more open to theatrical releases even after pulling out of its bid for Warner Bros. Discovery's studios and streaming businesses, extending Narnia: The Magician's Nephew's theater run from two weeks to seven.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: A theatrical shift is a positive for exhibitors and changes Netflix's windowing strategy.
insights.locator: Netflix is also being more open toward theater releases

insights.claim: Sarandos expects the sequel to KPop Demon Hunters, Netflix's most popular movie ever, to be huge in theaters and big on Netflix.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: A tentpole theatrical release would test Netflix's box-office plus streaming model.
insights.quote: “will be huge in theaters and big on Netflix.”
insights.locator: Netflix is also being more open toward theater releases
